newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan Oct leading index 83.3, coincident 90.0 - EPA.
newsitem.headline: Japan Oct leading index 83.3, coincident 90.0 - EPA.

text.p: Japan's diffusion index of leading economic indicators stood at 83.3 on a scale of 100 in October, rising above the so-called "boom or bust" mark of 50 for the second consecutive month, the Economic Planning Agency said on Tuesday.
A breakdown of the indices of economic indicators follows:
The EPA said in statement that the data shows the economy is continuing to recover.
A figure for the leading index above 50 is generally taken as suggesting the economy will expand in the coming months.
The coincident index measures current economic conditions, while the lagging index traces economic trends in the past few months.
It was the first time that all three indicators had simultaneously risen above 50 since February this year.
"We have taken half a step forward in our evaluation of the economy by dropping the phrase 'the basic trend' in describing the current recovery," a senior EPA official told reporters.
In the first half of the year, the EPA kept on saying that "the basic trend of the economy was one of recovery". This was partly because the lagging indicator was below the 50 mark for some months.
